# setup-start — the front door of a project

**Input:** optional `--rerun` to review and change existing answers. Runs before `prime`; it needs no primed context.

**Guardrails (absolute):** never read, create or test for `.env`; never touch `~/.claude/`, `~/.codex/` or any host-global setting; never delete files; never write the profile before the user approves the summary screen; never prune or edit the plugin cache — a disabled group is a profile flag, not a deletion; never overwrite a populated `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` or `.agents/project-rules.md` — `kept` is the only answer for an existing file; never shorten an existing `CLAUDE.md` (legacy gates read its `Validation`, `Branch model`, `Style & Conventions`, `Orchestrate publish` headings by name).

Contract and field docs: `references/setup-contract.md`. Templates: `templates/project-rules.md`, `templates/CLAUDE.md`, `templates/AGENTS.md`, `templates/memory/index.md` (and its siblings). Scripts: `scripts/profile.mjs` (profile), `scripts/rules.mjs` (rules authority + rendering), `scripts/bootstrap.mjs` (memory seed + readiness), `scripts/preflight-deps.mjs` (dependencies).

## Phase A — Interview

**A.0 Read state (never ask what the repo already says).** `git remote get-url origin`, `git branch --list`, file count, and `node <plugin_root>/scripts/profile.mjs read --project-root <project_root>`:

- `conflict` → print the differing keys and stop. Two disagreeing profiles are a human decision.
- `ok` → *Re-run* path: show the current effective values as a table; per screen ask keep/change.
- `missing` → interview. A missing profile means an interview; never infer team preferences from which CLIs happen to be installed on this machine.

**A.1 Screens** (one question set per screen, detected value pre-selected and marked *(Recommended)*; render in the language chosen on Screen 0):

- **Screen 0 — Language:** `pl` | `en` (conversation only; code and commits stay English).
- **Screen 1 — Project:** mode (greenfield/brownfield, detected ≥50 files → brownfield) · git host (from `origin`) · how code reaches main: (a) push to main → `trunk`, `pr_required=false` · (b) PR → `feature-branch` · (c) develop + release → `gitflow`. `custom` is not offered.
- **Screen 2 — Team tools:** tracker (`jira` | `none`) · Confluence (yes/no) · Codex used by the team as second opinion (yes/no — a team answer, the file is shared).
- **Screen 2b — Project facts (greenfield, or brownfield without a populated `CLAUDE.md`):** one-paragraph project description · validation command(s) (the real ones — a docs-only project has its own; never invent an npm/typecheck line) · dev/build/test commands · tech stack rows · one-paragraph architecture · style/linter pointer · sensitive paths and `lib` dir · rendered UI? (`app_surface`, `ui_paths`) · declared LSP (from the manifest, never from `command -v`) · docs hosts. Detected values are pre-filled and confirmed, never assumed. A brownfield project with a populated `CLAUDE.md` skips this screen: its rules are the authority.
- **Screen 3 — Harness roles:** author host you will mostly work from (`claude` | `codex`) · **independent review enabled for this team?** yes *(Recommended)* / no — an explicit team choice written to `groups.review`; `no` is a visible opt-out that every skill reports, never an opinion. With `yes`, state the required second CLI (the other host), its model and effort explicitly: reviewer for Claude authors: Codex model + effort (default `gpt-6-astra` / `high`); reviewer for Codex authors: Claude `fable` / `high`. Never infer from which CLIs happen to be installed on this machine that the team has them — a missing CLI later **blocks** the review, it does not silently opt out. · after an approved spec: **stop** *(Recommended)* or continue to `plan-feature` (`planning.after_brainstorm`) · executor role: Opus / `medium` (shown, not asked).
- **Screen 4 — Summary:** the full profile and the `groups` map derived below, plus *what I will create* / *what stays* / *manual steps*, and every **contradiction** the profile validator reports (`profile.mjs apply` without consent returns them: review enabled but Codex unused, tracker group on with tracker `none`, PR-gated preset with `push`). Resolve each one here — the screen cannot be approved while one stands. Options: **Approve and run** · **Change something** (re-ask that one question only). No new facts here.

**A.2 Derive.** `workflow.*` from the preset (trunk/integration/branch pattern/protected/merge per `references/setup-contract.md`); `orchestrate_publish` is derived by `scripts/rules.mjs` (`derivePublish`): `push` only for direct-to-trunk, `branch-local` for every PR-gated preset — never hand-set to `push`. `groups`: `planning=true`, `review=<Screen 3 answer>`, `execution=false` (deferred to the legacy release), `git=true` (commit / push / pull / release / pr-create / start-task ship in the plugin since 0.2.0; a project that keeps the legacy git commands sets it `false` explicitly), `tracker = tracker==jira`, `confluence = <answer>`. Legacy `commands.*` mirror is kept only when writing into a legacy schema-1 file (`profile.mjs` mirrors `codex`/`confluence` automatically).

## Phase B — Configure (after Approve; each step reports `created | kept | synced | skipped(<why>)`)

1. **Profile.** One atomic write of the whole approved profile: `node <plugin_root>/scripts/profile.mjs apply --project-root <root> --changes '<json of dotted keys>' --consent yes --create yes` (arrays and objects are JSON values — `workflow.protected`, `roles.reviewer.codex` — never strings). The whole result is validated before anything is written; a rejected batch leaves no partial profile. New project → canonical `.agents/project-profile.json`, schema 2. Only a legacy `.claude/project-profile.json` exists → the same command writes that file in place: schema 1 and every old or unknown key preserved, new fields under `harness`. Never create a second authoritative profile.
2. **Rules.** `node <plugin_root>/scripts/rules.mjs authority --project-root <root>` decides the path, then `rules.mjs render --project-root <root> --facts <facts.json> --consent yes` performs it (absent-only for rule bodies, never overwrites; the one exception is the generated compat `CLAUDE.md`, whose mirrored facts — validation command, `Orchestrate publish`, branch model, language — are re-synced from `.agents/project-rules.md` and reported as `synced`; a hand-written `CLAUDE.md` that differs is reported as `drift` and left alone):
   - **Brownfield** (a populated, hand-written `CLAUDE.md`): it stays the single authority, whole and untouched. `AGENTS.md` is rendered to load `CLAUDE.md`. **No `.agents/project-rules.md` is created** — a generic seed must not compete with the real rules. Fill only its `### Branch model` fields and the `Claude ↔ developer communication` cell if they are placeholders, exactly as the legacy command did.
   - **Greenfield**: `.agents/project-rules.md` is rendered from the confirmed facts (Screen 2b + profile) and is the authority; `CLAUDE.md` is rendered as a compatibility copy carrying every legacy heading and content line (`Validation`, `Git Workflow` with `**Orchestrate publish:**`, `### Branch model`, the worktree guard, `Language Rules`, `Commands`, `Code Structure & Modularity`, `Style & Conventions`, `Tech Stack`, `Automatic Behaviors`, `Search Commands`, `Security`, `Project Knowledge Layers`, `Error Handling`; `Code Navigation` only with a declared LSP; runtime smoke only with a rendered UI); `AGENTS.md` points at the shared rules.
   - **Conflict** (both files hand-written): stop; a human picks the authority.
   The render result says `ready: true` only when every required field is resolved (`validation-command`, `language`, `publish`, branch model) and the compat copy carries no `drift`. `created` is not `ready`: report `incomplete — unresolved: …` and keep asking until it is, never declare setup done with a placeholder validation command.
2b. **Memory layer.** `node <plugin_root>/scripts/bootstrap.mjs seed --project-root <root> --consent yes` — absent-only: routing (`index.md`), `reflection-protocol.md`, empty placeholders (brief, architecture, patterns, decisions, errors, api, domain/business-model), `user-profile.md.example`, and the `.agents/{specs,plans,reference,sources}` scaffold. Existing memory — populated or empty — is `kept` byte for byte. No project lesson, user data or starter incident is ever seeded.
3. **Binding.** For each host the user will use, bind the installed plugin: `node <plugin_root>/scripts/profile.mjs bind --project-root <root> --host <host> --plugin-root <installed root>` — the installed root is this plugin's own root for the current host; for the other host ask the operator for its installed root (or run the same command from that host). This verifies the package marker, payload digest, skill and hook paths, then writes the portable `.agents/harness-version.json` (identity only, committed) and the machine-local `.agents/harness-state/binding.json` (root, timestamp; gitignored). A clone on another machine must bind again — a copied receipt is not an installation. A schema-1 receipt → offer `profile.mjs migrate-binding --consent yes`. A failed verification is reported and left unbound. Hooks: binding installs nothing and trusts nothing; hook activation is a separate operator step (`references/installation.md → Activation`). **Claude Code only — script allowance.** After a successful bind, propose one machine-local permission so the plugin's scripts run without a prompt per call: `Bash(node <parent of the installed root>/*)` (the parent is the version-agnostic cache directory, e.g. `~/.claude/plugins/cache/ai-coding-starter/harness`; spell it as the absolute path, no leading wildcard). Write it into `.claude/settings.local.json → permissions.allow` only with consent, never into the shared `settings.json`: a portable glob would also allow a file the agent itself wrote under a matching path, which is why `settings.json` ships a deny on writes under `~/.claude/plugins/**` instead. Report `created | kept`.
3b. **Wrappers (Claude Code only).** `node <plugin_root>/scripts/bootstrap.mjs wrappers --project-root <root> --plugin-root <plugin_root>` previews `created | updated | kept` per wrapper (`templates/wrappers/*.md` → `.claude/commands/`), so the bare command (`/prime`, `/brainstorm`, `/commit`, …) routes to the plugin skill. A file marked `replaces_local_edit` holds project edits → show the diff and ask; then re-run with `--consent yes`. Wrappers are ordinary starter files (sync category A) — never record them as `migrated`, which means an intentional deletion. Namespaced commands (`/setup:start`, `/maintain:*`, `/gates:*`) get no wrapper; they are invoked as `/harness:<skill>`.
3b. **Dependency preflight.** `node <plugin_root>/scripts/preflight-deps.mjs --project-root <root> --host <host>`: node ≥ 22 and git are required (missing → the commit/push guards cannot run and will block; report it as missing protection), `jq` only matters for legacy Bash hooks. The project's own `.claude/hooks/check-project-deps.sh` runs unchanged with the project root as cwd and its output is relayed verbatim — never parsed, never exported.
3c. **Codex write access.** When the author host is (or may be) Codex: print the manual step — add the project's absolute `.agents` path to `sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots` in `~/.codex/config.toml`, or in `.codex/config.toml` once the project is trusted (`references/setup-contract.md → Codex sandbox and .agents/`). Never write `~/.codex/` yourself. Until this is done, Codex planning skills cannot save specs or plans.
4. **Legacy-only steps — route, do not perform.** `.env.example` toggles, `.mcp.json` pruning, toolchain block in `check-project-deps.sh`, command-group pruning, TESTING/DoD/PR templates belong to the legacy `/setup:start` (`.claude/commands/setup/start.md`). If that file exists in the project, print: `run /setup:start for: <list>`; if it does not, print `legacy bootstrap not installed in this project — skipped: <list>` and stop there. Never reconstruct those steps from memory.

## Phase C — Route (print, run nothing)

Greenfield: `prime` → (legacy PRD/brief commands if present) → `brainstorm` → `plan-feature` → execution stage (legacy). Brownfield: `prime` → (legacy `setup:map-codebase` if present) → `brainstorm`. State that the commands continue in this primed conversation or need `prime` after a fresh chat.

## Report

Profile summary (one line per field, `groups.review` with its explicit yes/no) · rules authority (`brownfield: CLAUDE.md` | `greenfield: .agents/project-rules.md`) and `ready` / `incomplete — unresolved: …` · Phase B table (never truncated) · memory seed counts (created / kept) · binding result per host (portable + local) · dependency preflight · legacy steps routed or skipped · Phase C list. `node <plugin_root>/scripts/bootstrap.mjs report --project-root <root> --host <host>` is the one readiness verdict to quote: blockers first, then warnings (an empty brief or architecture is a warning, never a blocker). Re-enabling a group is a profile change after confirmation; nothing is restored from or deleted in the plugin cache.
